title: incident-command-1on1-brief
content:
Purpose: quick prep for 1:1 with Marta (CS lead) before we enter incident command for Acme Corp perf regression. This is a focused pre-handoff to align on customer comms, immediate mitigations we can ask them to accept, and the three-hour action plan we will propose to execs.

Meeting goals:
- Align on single customer-facing message (ETA + ask + what we are doing). Keep it simple.
- Confirm agreed mitigation options we can implement during maintenance window.
- Agree timeboxed rollback/route to minimize token loss.
- Identify primary owners for each action item and cutover criteria.

Toplines to carve out (talking points)
- What happened (2-3 bullets): sudden spike in token-drop errors starting ~2026-03-10 02:15 UTC; latency increase for embeddings and text-gen on r4a nodes; auto-scaling failed to bring new nodes due to quota errors.
- Current impact: Acme sees 30–45% higher 95th pct latency, intermittent 500 errors for longer (>10s). Affects batch jobs and streaming endpoints.
- Short term ask from customer: tolerate brief maintenance (5–10 min) for instance restart + temp route to fallback model. Offer discounted tokens for downtime window.

Quick diagnostic notes (to reference during call)
- Metrics pages: /console/metrics/model/r4a - watch qps, cpu, nvlink errors.
- Logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/r4a/errors/2026-03-10/*.grep "KV cache fail"
- Recent deploys: infra PR #3482 (kernel upgrade) merged 2026-03-09 21:40 UTC — correlate to onset?
- Known flake: occasional NVLink reset on p4x nodes under heavy KV cache pressure (ops runbook flag).

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Kernel upgrade + KV cache pressure -> degraded NVLink behavior -> higher token retries -> latency + 5xx.
2) Autoscaler quota boundary + misconfigured scaling policy -> cold-start spikes -> queue saturation.
3) Customer workload changed (larger sequences) exposed a model path we don't optimize.

Immediate mitigations we can propose (fast, reversible)
- Temp route Acme traffic to fallback model (v1.9 quantized) that has lower mem footprint but slightly higher perplexity. Tradeoff: lower latency, potential quality regression. (Owner: Daniel)
- Manual scale-up of r4a pool by +2 instances and pause autoscaler for 30 min. (Owner: Noah)
- Set per-customer concurrency cap at 60 for next 2 hours to reduce queuing. (Owner: Jules)
- If kernel appears implicated, roll back infra PR #3482 on a canary host and run smoke tests. (Owner: platform-release)

Customer-facing messaging (single-sentence + ask)
- "We’re investigating elevated latency and intermittent errors affecting your inference; we propose a short maintenance window (5–10 min) to switch your traffic to a fallback model and scale capacity — can we proceed at T+30 min?"

Escalation ladder for this call
- Level 1: Jules (SRE) — handling immediate config changes and monitoring.
- Level 2: Marta (CS) — customer comms and approvals; legal if compensation required.
- Level 3: Daniel (Infra lead) — kernel/driver rollbacks and deeper diagnostics.
- Exec: Noah (Head SRE) — signoff for capacity spend > $X / hour or customer SLA credits.

Handoff checklist (what I need from Marta during 1:1)
- Clear permission to proceed with fallback-model switch + temp cap (yes/no).
- Point of contact at Acme (name, mobile) for immediate confirmation.
- Any contractual constraints about model substitutions or downtime.

Post-call commitments (draft to convert into tickets during/after incident command)
- TASK-1: implement traffic route to fallback model; perform smoke test within 5m. Owner: Daniel. ETA: T+20.
- TASK-2: manual scale r4a pool + pause autoscaler. Owner: Noah. ETA: T+10.
- TASK-3: enable per-customer concurrency cap for Acme for 2h. Owner: Jules. ETA: T+5.
- TASK-4: gather full kernel logs and link to INC-9203. Owner: platform-release. ETA: T+60.
- TASK-5: draft customer update and compensation options; include token credit estimate. Owner: Marta. ETA: T+30.

Notes to self (rough)
- Keep comms humble and specific — avoid promises about exact restore time unless we have a validated mitigation.
- If rollback is needed, ensure we have one canary host validated first.
- Watch cost run rate; manual scale is expensive beyond 45 min. Flag to Noah for > $1k estimate.

Open questions (to resolve in 1:1)
- Do we have legal constraints on model substitution for Acme? (Marta)
- Can NeoOps approve +2 r4a immediately or do we need procurement? (Noah)
- Is there an existing per-customer cap policy we can reuse or do we create a one-off? (Jules)

Prep checklist for the 1:1 (my quick tick-boxes)
- [ ] Slack thread drafted: #prod-ops -> short summary + link to this doc.
- [ ] Customer single-sentence drafted and pinned in the meeting.
- [ ] Fallback model tested on staging for same payload shape.
- [ ] Autoscaler toggle runbook open with steps and rollback.
- [ ] Billing/contact info for Acme (needed for compensation).

Tone/style notes for call: be calm, show data, offer a short mitigation path, confirm permission, then move to action. Avoid technical deep dives that will confuse CS — offer to follow up with separate deep-dive notes.

After-action quick template (what I will paste into the incident ticket after the call)
- Summary: (1–2 lines)
- Actions taken (list) + timestamps
- Current status and next steps
- Customer comms sent (copy)
- Owners and ETA for postmortem

-- end scratchpad --

(keeping this in users/ so I can iterate quickly; will move finalized notes into shared_drives/incident-postmortems after wrap-up)
